title: Ignition gateway / OPC server
purpose: Ignition as OPC server to tippers/hospital and tag provider (SYS1 metrics) feeding Aveva. L2/L3 use Gateway UI for OPC Connections and performance; L1 only identifies role/symptoms.

Heartbeat flatline on tippers after Ignition comes up late → restart OptiSweep.
Same APIs Ignition calls also available in Apidog on primary.
OPC COM module ties robotics path; XLE COM / Stunnel for UPS chat.

OptiSweep software environment overview: The source describes OptiSweep software as the software that 'integrates everything.' The slide and transcript identify AVEVA as the HMI and Ignition as the OPC server.

Ignition as the OPC server: The transcript states that Ignition is 'our OPC server.' The speaker also confirms that OPC is a protocol and refers to it as an industry standard protocol. The source further states that Ignition communicates through the tippers through OPC and feeds data to AVEVA because AVEVA can directly integrate with the OPC...

OptiSweep architecture overview: The architecture includes an XLe chat communication module, Sorter Sweeper module, Robotics module, Geek+ comm module, XLe chat OBC communication, sorter and tipper PLCs, Ignition OPC server, Aveva HMI, SQL Server, scanners, ASX, and printers.

OPC COM module and tag communication: The transcript states that the OPC COM module manages communication between the Robotics module and the Geek Plus RMS server. It also uses Ignition's built-in tag provider to connect to the hospital and tippers and relay relevant tags.

Primary services required for OptiSweep system operation: Ignition is used for OPC connections, Stunnel provides secure encryption for communication to the UPS Xle chat, and OptiSweep is Fortna's service that coordinates all operations.

OptiSweep System Overview: The system directs parcels from the sorter into totes. When a tote reaches a customer-specified weight, parcel count, or volume, the WCS signals the sorter PLC to stop diverting. An AGV retrieves the full tote and another AGV places an empty tote. The WCS then signals the sorter PLC to resume sorting.

OptiSweep WCS and Sorter PLC Interaction: Once the sorter starts, parcels are directed into totes. When the tote reaches the customer-specified weight, number of parcels, or volume, the WCS sends a message to the sorter PLC to stop diverting packages. An AGV is triggered via the WCS controller to retrieve the tote.

OptiSweep WCS Controller: The WCS controller manages the flow of totes by sending messages to the sorter PLC to stop or resume diverting packages based on tote weight, parcel count, or volume. It triggers AGVs to retrieve full totes and place empty ones. It directs AGVs to open tippers or the hospital station based on operational status.
OptiSweep System Control: The ACB API Screen provides an interface for controlling the OptiSweep system. The specific controls available are not detailed in this section.

OptiSweep System Operation Overview: The system's automated operation is managed by the WCS. Operators only need to interact manually with the system at the tipper and hospital stations. The provided procedures in the manual apply specifically to these two station types.

OptiSweep software structure described as state machines and communication modules: In response to a question about whether charging is a separate module, the speaker says it is one software system under the Opti umbrella and not a separate model.

Sorter Sweeper module: The module tracks packages as they come in, updates associated information, and tracks the tote at the tipper. It makes requests to the Robotics module for actions such as picking up a tote, moving a tote out, and dropping off a tote.

Robotics and Geek+ communication integration: The Sorter Sweeper module sends requests such as pick up tote, move out tote, and drop off tote to the Robotics module. The Robotics module runs these requests through configured maps, including sorter and tipper queue and execution areas.

Sorter Sweeper module architecture and responsibilities: Sorter Sweeper receives data from sorter tippers, hospital stations, and the HMI; creates tote tasks for the Sorter Robotics module; processes data from the hospital; and notifies tippers about tote arrivals or robot faults.

Sorter Robotics module and AGV task interface: Sorter Robotics receives tote tasks from Sorter Sweeper and generates commands for Geek Plus. The transcript lists AGV-related commands including initialize AGV, empty, go to, pick up tote, move tote, drop off tote, cancel request, and go charge.

Database Walkthrough: The provided source identifies a training video slide labeled "Database Walkthrough" and does not provide further operational details about the database, its screens, or its use.

Geek+ Communication Module: The diagram shows the Geek+ Comm Module alongside the Robotics and SorterSweeper modules. The Robotics module generates commands for Geek+ to execute tote tasks, and the diagram includes robot notifications and command results among the related message concepts.
Database Tables: The transcript refers collectively to “all the tables.” The source does not identify individual tables or describe their contents, relationships, retention, or usage.

OPC connection configuration and subscribed tags: The OPC configuration table stores connection parameters required for the software to bridge to OPC. The OPC tags table stores tags that are subscribed to at startup. The training describes these records as covering the information required to connect to OPC and the tags that are written to and read from.

Vendor-agnostic robot command model: The Robotics module sends generic commands such as moving a tote to a drop-off location. The Geek Plus COM module translates these internal commands into the vendor platform's REST API format and converts responses back into the format used by OptiSweep.

OptiSweep robotics database landscape: The database view shows multiple Helix2x_1Prod databases, including Audit, DataContainers, EntityLogs, GeekAgv, OpcComms, PlcCommunication, and Robotics. The segment transcript also states that there is not just one system.

Tag variable types and value storage: The transcript states that tags can have different data types and are commonly represented as strings in the tag model. A variable type identifies which value representation or column applies to a particular tag.
